source.title: Null-Space Constrained Low-Rank Adaptation for Response-Specified Large Language Model Unlearning
source.authors: Bo-Cheng Ju; Jianhua Wang; Chengliang Liu; Xiao-Lin Chang

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own results on format-shifted and prompt-based recovery evaluations and argues that suppression persists under the tested prompt variations, with limited recovery under jailbreak wrappers.
record.gate_note: The paper tests prompt-format shifts, multilingual prompts, and jailbreak-style wrappers on its own NSRU method and reports baseline unlearning-method results under TOFU format shifts. It does not test fine-tuning recovery, activation-direction ablation, or quantization. Cited claims about downstream fine-tuning are not results of this study.
record.test_reason: A new-method paper (NSRU) that reports its own results on near-chance WMDP accuracy with utility kept, plus prompt-only recovery attempts (multilingual prompts, jailbreak wrappers, ReLU format shifts). These bear on A, E and F in a new method setting. It has no fine-tuning, activation-ablation or quantization attacks.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that NSRU suppresses hazardous and forget-set knowledge (near-random WMDP accuracy, zero ES on TOFU) while preserving utility better than baselines, and that suppression persists under the tested format, multilingual and jailbreak variations with only limited jailbreak recovery. On Bio the jailbreak maximum (26.55%) is actually below the English unlearned score. The paper does not test fine-tuning, ablation or quantization recovery.
record.recipe_differences: NSRU combines safe-target supervision, undesired-response suppression, retain loss, and null-space constrained LoRA updates; it is not a direct reproduction of the unlearning recipes named in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Prompt variation changes WMDP accuracy: jailbreak wrappers yield higher reported maxima than multilingual prompts. TOFU results vary by unlearning method; NSRU has the lowest F-Odd value in Table VI.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablation on TOFU-Forget05: training only on the safe target without undesired-response suppression gives high ST-ROUGE (0.87) but ES of 0.83. The model imitates the refusal while the original answer remains extractable.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal-style target training alone produces surface suppression that leaves forgotten answers extractable.

fits_no_version.finding: In the authors' reimplementation, RMU on Zephyr-7B collapses MMLU to about 0.23 on both WMDP subsets, contrary to the original WMDP report.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Utility preservation of RMU depends on implementation and hyperparameters.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported. The text gives aggregate ranges or maxima rather than individual multilingual and jailbreak-wrapper values; Figure 5 contains the plotted condition-level results. TOFU format-shift scores have no unlearned-model or chance reference in the reported table, limiting interpretation of their absolute magnitudes.
record.rows_left_out: None. Table VI's retain-side transformed-format metrics (R-MCQA, R-Cloze, and R-CQA) were omitted because they measure retained capability rather than forget-split recovery or the attack outcomes in the claim.

untested.parts: No relearning or fine-tuning attack on any unlearned model.
No activation-direction ablation, probing, or analysis of whether knowledge is deleted or blocked.
No in-context information attacks, no adaptive or optimized jailbreaks (only three fixed wrappers), and no WMDP prompt attacks on the baseline methods.
NSRU resistance to fine-tuning, ablation and quantization attacks is untested. Only fixed prompt variations were tried, on one model per benchmark.
Only one backbone (Zephyr-7B) on WMDP. No probing or extraction beyond multiple-choice accuracy on WMDP.

missing.what: WMDP accuracy, MMLU and Adj-MMLU for baseline methods (GradAscent, GradDiff, NPO, RMU, TRU)
TOFU Extraction Strength (ES) and Forget Quality for all methods, including NSRU ES = 0 on Forget05/Forget10 and Base ES 0.957
Per-language and per-wrapper WMDP accuracies, and the English reference used for the stress test

record.verdict_notes: This is a method paper. Verdicts rest on fixed, non-adaptive prompt attacks on a single model, with no uncertainty reported. The record wrongly used random choice rather than the unlearned English accuracy as the baseline for the jailbreak rows, and wrongly marked the ReLU NSRU rows as partial. The text and Table III disagree on English Cyber accuracy (27.23% vs 27.73%).

versions.untested_parts: Tests NSRU on WMDP hazardous-domain accuracy and utility, with prompt stress tests; does not establish the same result for all unlearning methods or attack types.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or small-set relearning attack is reported.
No activation-direction ablation attack or analysis showing that NSRU blocks access rather than deleting knowledge is reported.
Tests TOFU format transformations, WMDP Chinese, Spanish, and Russian prompts, and three jailbreak-style wrappers; does not test every rephrasing, language, or in-context-information attack.
Tests NSRU against prompt-format, multilingual, and jailbreak-style variations only; does not test resistance to fine-tuning, activation ablation, or quantization.

relation.reason: It reports its own WMDP and prompt-only recovery results bearing on A, E and F.

tranche.reason: It uses the WMDP original's model (Zephyr-7B-beta), benchmark (WMDP-Bio/Cyber) and measures (WMDP and MMLU accuracy) but a different unlearning method plus prompt attacks. That is a different method on the same question, not a new setting.

source_check.notes: The Fig. 5 stress-test text and Table III disagree on English Cyber (27.23% vs 0.2773), and no English Bio value is given for Fig. 5. So comparing the Bio jailbreak maximum (26.55%) with Table III's 0.2726 is unsafe; the authors report a limited jailbreak rise in both domains. The pack's authors_conclusion repeats the 'Bio below English' reading. No per-language or per-wrapper values, one model per benchmark, no uncertainty, no code.
